glosses: to damn (to condemn as unfit etc.)
skazywać, potępiać
Condamner aux peines de l’enfer, punir des peines de l’enfer.

examples.text: Dieu damnera les méchants.

glosses: Rendre digne des peines de l’enfer.

examples.text: Elle revint habillée d’un tailleur noir, hyper-sexy, la veste bâillant sur une poitrine à damner un intégriste.
Damner son âme.

glosses: Déclarer une personne digne des peines de l’enfer.

examples.text: Il ne faut damner personne.

glosses: Ce qui cause beaucoup d’impatience ou dont on est extrêmement tourmenté.

examples.text: Cela me fait, me ferait damner,
Sa lenteur me fait damner.
Il a une femme qui le fait damner.

glosses: S’exposer à être damné, à mériter les peines de l’enfer.

examples.text:
Tout ce qui est mal… C’est bon… Alors ?
Tout ce qui est bon… C’est mal… Alors ?
Damne-toi ! damne-toi ?

glosses: To condemn.

examples.text: The official position is that anyone who does this will be damned for all eternity.
Only God can damn.
I damn you eternally, fiend!

glosses: To condemn; to declare guilty; to doom; to adjudge to punishment.

examples.text: He shall not live; look, with a spot I damn him.
Lack of access to support services can damn children with disabilities and lesser means to lives where they never harness their full range of abilities.

glosses: To put out of favor; to ruin; to label negatively.

examples.text: I’m afraid that if I speak out on this, I’ll be damned as a troublemaker.

glosses: To condemn as unfit, harmful, invalid, immoral or illegal.

examples.text:
1708 November 8, Alexander Pope, letter to Henry Cromwell
You are not so arrant a critic as to damn them [the works of modern poets] […] without hearing.
Homosexuality and suicide have some common characteristics. Both are damned by the Western Judeo-Christian culture as sins (although the latter has only been considered such since the sixth century).

glosses: To curse; put a curse upon.

examples.text: That man stole my wallet. Damn him!

glosses: To invoke damnation; to curse.

examples.text:
c. 1767-1774, Oliver Goldsmith, letter to Mrs. Bunbury
[…] while I inwardly damn.

glosses: Generic intensifier. Fucking; bloody.

examples.text: Shut the damn door!
Damn freaks!
Damn psychos!
The whole damn building came down!
Damn cultists are psychotic.
Where's that damn FOURTH Chaos Emerald!

glosses: Very; extremely.

examples.text: That car was going damn fast!
How are you damn quick?
You must be so damn rapid.
I damn well hope you never come back.
We're begging, damn near down on our knees, and not getting one red cent.

glosses: Used to express anger, irritation, disappointment, annoyance, contempt or surprise, etc. See also dammit.
The word \"damn\" employed as a curse.

examples.text: He said a few damns and left.

glosses: A small, negligible quantity, being of little value; a whit or jot.

examples.text: The new hires aren't worth a damn.

glosses: The smallest amount of concern or consideration.

examples.text: I don't give a damn.
